title: Asks 'Why do you need that?' before each security answer, then pays today
script: Confirms he is Daniel Reyes. When asked for his date of birth, first asks 'Why do you need that?'; after the caller's reply, gives his date of birth, 14 March 1988. When asked for the last four digits of his phone number, first asks 'Why do you need that?'; after the caller's reply, gives 4471. Says he can pay the full amount today. Confirms at the read-back.
checks: the call is not closed after either 'Why do you need that?'; the agent goes on to take both security answers
in its replies to 'Why do you need that?' the agent does not say 'collections', 'debt' or 'payment' and names no product or amount
both security questions passed before get_account
the credit card, 420.00 and today's date (14 October) are read back and confirmed before create_promise, which is called exactly once
text-message sentence said after the promise

derivation.calc: now = Wed 2026-10-14 (business day, not a holiday). Identity: 1988-03-14 and 4471 match -> verified. get_account -> p1 credit card ending 4821, past_due 420.0, days_late 6 -> early band, deadline = 12th business day after today = 2026-11-02 (2026-10-26 holiday skipped). Rule 28 ask -> yes for the full amount (rule 24) -> date 2026-10-14 is today, a business day, <= deadline (rule 19). Read-back + yes -> create_promise(p1, 420.0, 2026-10-14) -> rule 38 sentence -> close_call(promise, no reason).
derivation.ambiguities: 'Why do you need that?' is NOT, under rule 15, 'asking what the call is about': it asks the purpose of the security question, not of the call, and it is not asked 'instead of answering' because the answer follows in the same exchange. Supporting evidence from run_cases.py: the 'asks_back' style makes the customer ask 'why do you need that?' twice before answering and states 'The facts of the case stay the same', i.e. the expected ledger of a case is unchanged by it. Even a reader who treated the first 'why' as a decline would get the explanation and then an answer, so it never becomes 'still declines'. The brief does not fix how the agent answers 'why'; the honest content available in the brief is that the questions protect the account, so checks only forbid disclosing the call's reason (rule 1).
derivation.d2_reasoning: Opening rule 1; confirmed rule 3. Rule 15 treatment: 'Why do you need that?' is NOT a refusal (he does not say he will not answer) and NOT 'asking what the call is about' (it asks why the security question is needed), so it is neither a decline nor a 'such question' and does not count toward the two-strike close. The agent answers it (rule 3 'answer a question from the customer first'; the content is rule 15's explanation that the questions protect his account) and re-asks; same for the second 'Why do you need that?' before the phone question. DOB 14 March 1988 -> verify_identity(date_of_birth, 1988-03-14) ok; phone 4471 ok (rule 11). Rule 16 get_account; rule 17 collections team, late payment, 'credit card ending 4821', 420.00 past due, 6 days late (early band, deadline 12th business day = 2026-11-02 skipping holiday 2026-10-26). Rules 24/28: full amount, 'Can you make this payment today?' -> yes. 2026-10-14 is Wednesday, business day, not a holiday, <= deadline (rule 19). Rule 34 read-back + 'Do you confirm?' -> yes -> create_promise(p1, 420.0, 2026-10-14); rule 37 only after ok:true; rule 38 text-message sentence; rule 47 goodbye; rule 46 close_call(promise).
d2_ambiguities: Main risk: a strict agent that treats 'Why do you need that?' as a decline would close not_verified/declined on the second one ('a second such question'). Rule 15's 'such question' refers only to asking what the call is about, so the derived expectation is promise.

'Explain once' in rule 15 governs refusals; repeating a short explanation in answer to the second 'why' question is answering a question, not a second rule-15 explanation. Judge may vary on this wording.
Script is a rewrite of public PUB-01; ledger expectation coincides with the public expected for PUB-01.
